column1: Bats have a problem: how to find their way around in the dark.
column2: 蝙蝠有个难题：在黑暗中怎样辨路？
column5: find their way around|辨认方向；找到路

column1: They hunt at night, and cannot use light to help them find prey and avoid obstacles.
column2: 它们在夜间捕猎，无法靠光线寻找猎物或避开障碍。

column1: You might say that this is a problem of their own making, one that they could avoid simply by changing their habits and hunting by day.
column2: 你也许会说，这是蝙蝠自己造成的问题；只消改变习性，改在白天捕猎，它们就能避开这个问题。
column4: of their own making|自己造成的

column1: But the daytime economy is already heavily exploited by other creatures such as birds.
column2: 可是，白天可供谋生的资源早已被鸟类等其他生物充分利用了。
column3: daytime economy|白天可供生物利用的生存资源

column1: Given that there is a living to be made at night, and given that alternative daytime trades are thoroughly occupied, natural selection has favoured bats that make a go of the night-hunting trade.
column2: 夜间有谋生的机会，而白天可选的谋生方式又早已被占尽，在这种条件下，自然选择有利于那些能靠夜间捕猎生存的蝙蝠。
column4: a living to be made|有谋生的机会
column11: make a go of|成功经营；在此指靠……生存

column1: It is probable that the nocturnal trades go way back in the ancestry of all mammals.
column2: 很可能，所有哺乳动物的祖先很早就已靠夜间活动谋生。
column6: go way back|可追溯到很久以前

column1: In the time when the dinosaurs dominated the daytime economy, our mammalian ancestors probably only managed to survive at all because they found ways of scraping a living at night.
column2: 在恐龙主宰白天的生存空间时，我们的哺乳动物祖先之所以能活下来，很可能全靠它们找到了在夜间勉强维生的办法。
column4: daytime economy|白天争夺生存资源的活动

column1: Only after the mysterious mass extinction of the dinosaurs about 65 million years ago were our ancestors able to emerge into the daylight in any substantial numbers.
column2: 直到大约6500万年前恐龙神秘地大规模灭绝之后，我们的祖先中才有相当多的个体开始在白天活动。
column11: in any substantial numbers|以相当大的数量

column1: Bats have an engineering problem: how to find their way and find their prey in the absence of light.
column2: 蝙蝠面临一个工程学难题：没有光，怎样既能辨路又能找到猎物？
column6: in the absence of|在缺少……的情况下

column1: Bats are not the only creatures to face this difficulty today.
column2: 如今，面对这一难题的生物远不止蝙蝠。

column1: Obviously the night-flying insects that they prey on must find their way about somehow.
column2: 显然，那些在夜间飞行、被蝙蝠捕食的昆虫，也一定有某种辨路的方法。
column8: find their way about|辨别方向

column1: Deep-sea fish and whales have little or no light by day or by night.
column2: 无论白天还是黑夜，深海鱼和鲸所处的环境都几乎没有光，甚至完全无光。
column5: little or no|少得几乎没有，甚至完全没有
column6: by day or by night|无论白天还是夜晚

column1: Fish and dolphins that live in extremely muddy water cannot see because, although there is light, it is obstructed and scattered by the dirt in the water.
column2: 生活在极其浑浊的水中的鱼和海豚看不见东西，因为尽管有光，光也被水里的泥沙遮挡并散射了。

column1: Plenty of other modern animals make their living in conditions where seeing is difficult or impossible.
column2: 今天还有许多其他动物生活在很难甚至根本看不见东西的环境中。
column5: make their living|谋生；在此指生存

column1: Given the questions of how to manoeuvre in the dark, what solutions might an engineer consider?
column2: 要解决怎样在黑暗中自如行动的问题，工程师可能会考虑哪些办法？

column1: The first one that might occur to him is to manufacture light, to use a lantern or a searchlight.
column2: 他最先想到的办法或许是造出光来，比如用一盏提灯或探照灯。

column1: Fireflies and some fish (usually with the help of bacteria) have the power to manufacture their own light, but the process seems to consume a large amount of energy.
column2: 萤火虫和某些鱼能够自己发光（通常靠细菌帮忙），但这个过程似乎要消耗大量能量。
column4: with the help of|在……的帮助下
column6: have the power to|有能力做……

column1: Fireflies use their light for attracting mates.
column2: 萤火虫用光来吸引配偶。

column1: This doesn’t require a prohibitive amount of energy: a male’s tiny pinprick of light can be seen by a female from some distance on a dark night, since her eyes are exposed directly to the light source itself.
column2: 这样做所需的能量并不高到难以承受。漆黑的夜里，雌萤即使隔着一段距离，也能看见雄萤发出的一丁点光，因为它的眼睛直接面对光源本身。
column7: pinprick of light|针尖般的一点亮光
column9: from some distance|隔着一段距离
column11: exposed directly to|直接面对；直接接触

column1: However, using light to find one’s own way around requires vastly more energy, since the eyes have to detect the tiny fraction of the light that bounces off each part of the scene.
column2: 然而，用光来为自己辨路需要的能量大得多，因为眼睛得察觉到从眼前景物各个部分反射回来的那一小部分光。
column3: find one’s own way around|自己辨路
column8: tiny fraction|n. 极小的一部分

column1: The light source must therefore be immensely brighter if it is to be used as a headlight to illuminate the path, than if it is to be used as a signal to others.
column2: 因此，光源要是用作照亮前路的头灯，就必须比仅仅用来向其他个体发信号时亮得多。

column1: In any event, whether or not the reason is the energy expense, it seems to be the case that, with the possible exception of some weird deep-sea fish, no animal apart from man uses manufactured light to find its way about.
column2: 不管怎样，无论原因是否在于能量消耗，情况似乎是这样：除人类以外，没有动物靠自己造出的光来辨路，不过某些奇特的深海鱼可能是例外。
column6: seems to be the case|情况似乎如此
column7: with the possible exception of|……可能是例外

column1: What else might the engineer think of?
column2: 工程师还可能想出什么办法呢？

column1: Well, blind humans sometimes seem to have an uncanny sense of obstacles in their path.
column2: 有时，盲人似乎有一种异乎寻常的本领，能觉察前方道路上的障碍。
column9: in their path|在前进的路上

column1: It has been given the name ‘facial vision’, because blind people have reported that it feels a bit like the sense of touch, on the face.
column2: 这种感觉被称为“面部视觉”，因为有盲人说，感觉有点像是脸上的触觉。
column3: has been given the name|被称为

column1: One report tells of a totally blind boy who could ride his tricycle at good speed round the block near his home, using facial vision.
column2: 有一则报告说，一个双目完全失明的男孩凭借面部视觉，能骑着三轮车以相当快的速度绕家附近的街区一圈。
column8: at good speed|以相当快的速度

column1: Experiments showed that, in fact, facial vision is nothing to do with touch or the front of the face, although the sensation may be referred to the front of the face, like the referred pain in a phantom limb.
column2: 实验表明，面部视觉其实与触觉或脸部正面毫无关系，尽管人可能会觉得这种感觉来自脸部正面，就像幻肢中的牵涉痛一样。
column5: nothing to do with|与……毫无关系
column9: referred to|感觉被定位于另一部位

column1: The sensation of facial vision, it turns out, really goes in through the ears.
column2: 原来，这种所谓面部视觉的感觉，实际上是从耳朵传入的。

column1: Blind people, without even being aware of the fact, are actually using echoes of their own footsteps and of other sounds, to sense the presence of obstacles.
column2: 盲人甚至并未意识到，自己其实是在借助脚步声和其他声音的回声，感知前方是否有障碍物。
column3: without even being aware of|甚至没有意识到

column1: Before this was discovered, engineers had already built instruments to exploit the principle, for example to measure the depth of the sea under a ship.
column2: 在这一现象被发现之前，工程师就已经制造出利用这个原理的仪器，例如用它测量船下的水深。

column1: After this technique had been invented, it was only a matter of time before weapons designers adapted it for the detection of submarines.
column2: 这项技术发明之后，武器设计者将它改用于探测潜艇，就只是时间问题了。
column5: only a matter of time|只是时间问题

column1: Both sides in the Second World War relied heavily on these devices, under such codenames as Asdic (British) and Sonar (American), as well as Radar (American) or RDF (British), which uses radio echoes rather than sound echoes.
column2: 二战期间，交战双方都十分依赖这类装置，它们的代号有英国的 Asdic 和美国的 Sonar，还有美国称作 Radar、英国称作 RDF 的雷达；雷达利用的是无线电波的回波，而非声音的回声。
column4: Second World War|n. 第二次世界大战
column9: radio echoes|n. 无线电波的回波

column1: The Sonar and Radar pioneers didn’t know it then, but all the world now knows that bats, or rather natural selection working on bats, had perfected the system tens of millions of years earlier, and their ‘radar’ achieves feats of detection and navigation that would strike an engineer dumb with admiration.
column2: 当年的声呐和雷达先驱并不知道，如今却已人所共知：蝙蝠，更准确地说是作用于蝙蝠的自然选择，在数千万年前就已使这套系统臻于完善。蝙蝠用自己的“雷达”完成的探测与导航壮举，足以让工程师佩服得说不出话。
column12: strike an engineer dumb|使工程师惊叹得说不出话

column1: It is technically incorrect to talk about bat ‘radar’, since they do not use radio waves.
column2: 严格说来，把蝙蝠的这种能力称为“雷达”并不准确，因为蝙蝠并不使用无线电波。

column1: It is sonar.
column2: 它用的是声呐。
column3: sonar|n. 声呐；利用声波回声定位

column1: But the underlying mathematical theories of radar and sonar are very similar, and much of our scientific understanding of the details of what bats are doing has come from applying radar theory to them.
column2: 但雷达和声呐所依据的数学理论十分相似。对于蝙蝠究竟如何定位，许多细节上的科学认识来自人们把雷达理论应用到蝙蝠身上。

column1: The American zoologist Donald Griffin, who was largely responsible for the discovery of sonar in bats, coined the term ‘echolocation’ to cover both sonar and radar, whether used by animals or by human instruments.
column2: 美国动物学家唐纳德·格里芬对发现蝙蝠的声呐能力起了主要作用。他创造了“回声定位”这个术语，用来统称声呐和雷达，无论是动物还是人造仪器使用的。
